questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses inversion with *not only* and *but also* to emphasise a complex clause?
options: Not only had she finished the report, but also she had drafted the presentation slides before lunch.
She had not only finished the report but also drafted the presentation slides before lunch.
Had she not only finished the report but also drafted the presentation slides before lunch.
She finished the report and drafted the presentation slides before lunch, not only because of her teamwork.
questions.answer: She had not only finished the report but also drafted the presentation slides before lunch.

questions.question: Which cleft sentence correctly restates the subject of the original sentence as *it is* the person who completes the task?
options: It is the deadline that she must meet, not the task itself.
It is the task that she is assigned, and it is the deadline that she must meet.
It is she who completes the task on time, not the deadline.
It is the deadline that she must meet, which is what she finds challenging.
questions.answer: It is she who completes the task on time, not the deadline.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses a third conditional with *would have* to express regret about a past situation?
options: If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
If she had studied harder, she would study harder now.
If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam last year.
If she had studied harder, she would have been able to attend the lecture.
questions.answer: If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the subjunctive *were* to express a hypothetical scenario about a non-existent fact?
options: If I were you, I would take the job despite the risks.
If I were you, I would have taken the job before.
If I were you, I would have considered the job more seriously.
If I were you, I would have asked for more details.
questions.answer: If I were you, I would take the job despite the risks.

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates correct ellipsis of a repeated phrase in a formal context, maintaining coherence?
options: The conference was well-attended by academics, and the papers were discussed extensively, *as well as* the keynote speaker’s insights.
The conference was well-attended by academics, and the papers were discussed extensively, *and so were* the keynote speaker’s insights.
The conference was well-attended by academics, and the papers were discussed extensively, *which included* the keynote speaker’s insights.
The conference was well-attended by academics, and the papers were discussed extensively, *including* the keynote speaker’s insights.
questions.answer: The conference was well-attended by academics, and the papers were discussed extensively, *and so were* the keynote speaker’s insights.
